newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Noble leek becomes symbol of Albanian protest.
newsitem.headline: Noble leek becomes symbol of Albanian protest.

text.p: After Albanian protesters attacked Deputy Prime Minister Tritan Shehu with leeks last month, the cheap vegetable has become a defiant symbol of popular unrest across the impoverished Balkan country.

On the 12th day of street protests, sparked by the collapse of dubious investment schemes, protesters in this southern port town waved leeks at assembled television cameras and chanted: "Down with the leek government".
The main opposition alliance, the Forum for Democracy, has made the motto of its anti-government campaign: "Flowers not stones".
But fresh flowers are rare so demonstrators have started to brandish the more readily available vegetable.

Leeks were produced as a symbol after Shehu, chairman of the ruling Democratic Party, was seized upon by an angry crowd of beggared investors when he tried to address them at a stadium in Lushnje 60 kms (35 miles) to the north.
Witnesses said Shehu, his face bloodied in the melee by leek wielding protesters, barely escaped with his life. He managed to flee to the stadium changing rooms.
A helicopter dispatched to rescue him was prevented from landing and seven hours later Shehu sneaked out through a back door.
The incident enraged the government but emboldened many protesters, who proclaimed the leek their rowdy symbol.
President Sali Berisha was still visibly angry about the incident when he addressed supporters on Saturday and said those responsible for manhandling Shehu would be punished.

Destitute Albanians blame Berisha and the right-wing government of Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi for letting the high-risk pyramid schemes flourish unchecked and then standing by idly when they collapsed in January.
In what has become a daily routine in Vlore, protesters set fire to tyres in the town square before starting their march down the main street shouting "Berisha and Shehu, you are the biggest leeks".
Borrowing symbols from protests in Serbia, they also raise the three-finger Serbian salute to express their will to defy the government.
A group of protesters waved a bunch of 16 leeks, saying they symbolised the ministers in Meksi's cabinet.
Opposition newspapers have also seized on the colourful symbolism and are now calling on residents of the capital in Tirana to adopt the vegetable as their symbol, too.
So far demonstrations in the capital have been stopped by police before they could start and protests of any kind are rare in Tirana.
The opposition daily newspaper Koha Jone called on Sunday for demonstrators to rally in Tirana and other towns "With leeks in the square. Leeks instead of stones.
